claims.text: In-situ cryogenic cooling during AlCrFeNiSi additive manufacturing will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
In-situ cryogenic cooling will refine the microstructure of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ cryogenic cooling will improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing of the feedstock produces steep thermal gradients.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing produces high residual stresses.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the mechanical performance of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Machine-learning algorithms can dynamically adjust cryogenic cooling rates using in-situ temperature and stress feedback.
Laser powder bed fusion or a similar additive-manufacturing process is applicable to millimeter-scale AlCrFeNiSi components.
Maintaining local temperatures between -50 °C and -150 °C is an applicable cryogenic processing window.
Suppressing steep thermal gradients will produce a more uniform grain-size distribution.
Microstructural refinement will reduce stress-concentration sites.
Rapidly lowering the temperature of each deposited layer will reduce the thermal gradient between layers.
Reducing interlayer thermal gradients will minimize residual-stress formation.
Reducing interlayer thermal gradients will minimize unfavorable microstructural features.
Machine-learning control will optimize cooling separately for each layer despite variations in temperature and stress development.
Cryogenically processed components will have higher ductility than conventionally processed components.
Cryogenically processed components will have higher yield strength than conventionally processed components.
Integrating stress relief into the build will simplify the overall processing route.
The effectiveness of the intervention may require adjustment for larger geometries or different alloy systems.
